question: Let \(f(x)=ax^7+bx^3+cx-5,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are constants. If \(f(-7)=7,\) then \(f(7)\) equals
solution:
All the nonconstant powers are odd. Replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) therefore reverses the sign of every nonconstant term, while the constant remains \(-5\). Adding the two expressions cancels all terms containing the unknown coefficients:
\[
f(x)+f(-x)=-5-5=-10.
\]
Taking \(x=7\) and using \(f(-7)=7\), we obtain
\[
f(7)=-10-f(-7)=-10-7=\boxed{-17}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
